subject: Yes, SIR
alt: Cartoon: a headless body stained with blood, labelled democracy, stands upright. Beside it a smiling man in a black suit, with Gyanesh Kumar written on his coat, holds a sword and the severed head. Above it is written: Yes, SIR.
chutki: This is the bitterest cartoon of the series, and perhaps the most necessary. The body of democracy stands in kurta-pyjama and bare feet, the democracy of the ordinary person. Its head is in someone else's hand, and that hand is smiling.

Dhodapkar ties the saluting 'Yes, Sir' to the SIR process and tells the whole story in one word: obeying orders and cutting names from the rolls, both with the same sword. The cartoon shows blood so that we remember that a deleted vote is not a matter of paper; it is someone's voice being cut off.
